Let $y={e}^{\lambda x}.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {e}^{\lambda x},\,{y}^{″}={\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}-2\lambda {e}^{\lambda x}+2{e}^{\lambda x} & =0 \\ {e}^{\lambda x}({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The auxiliary equation is therefore

$$
{\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +2=0.
$$

The auxiliary equation can be solved by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +2 & =0 \\ ({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +1)-1+2 & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)^{2}+1 & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)^{2} & =-1 \\ \lambda -1 & =\pm \text{i} \\ \lambda  & =1\pm \text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation is

$$
y={e}^{x}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡x).
$$

Now let's find the constants $P$ and $Q.$ 

Substituting $y(0)=-2$ into the general solution gives

$$
P=-2.
$$

So we have

$$
y={e}^{x}(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡x).
$$

We now need to apply the condition ${y}^{′}(0)=-4.$ We differentiate $y$ to find ${y}^{′}$:

$$
{y}^{′}={e}^{x}(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+{e}^{x}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+Q\operatorname{cos}⁡x)
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(0)=-4$ into the above gives

$$
-2+Q=-4\,⟹\,Q=-2.
$$

So we have $P=-2$ and $Q=-2.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=-2{e}^{x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x).
$$
